Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the loss values for two experiments (Ex1 and Ex2) across training steps, showing both training and validation loss. The x-axis is labeled "Step" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60000, with tick labels at intervals of 10000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and employs a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 x 10<sup>1</sup> to 1.2 x 10<sup>1</sup>, with tick labels at intervals of 1 x 10<sup>1</sup>. The first line, representing "Ex1 Loss", is blue with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 1.1 x 10<sup>1</sup> at Step 0, decreases to approximately 1.8 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 10000, and then plateaus around 1.9 x 10<sup>0</sup> for the remaining steps up to Step 60000. The second line, representing "Ex2 Loss", is green with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 6 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 0, decreases to approximately 2.2 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 10000, and then gradually declines to approximately 1.7 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 60000. The third line, representing "Ex1 Validation Loss", is blue with dashed markers and a dashed line style; it begins at approximately 6 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 0, decreases to approximately 3.3 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 10000, and remains relatively stable around 3.1 x 10<sup>0</sup> to 3.2 x 10<sup>0</sup> for the remainder of the x-axis. The fourth line, representing "Ex2 Validation Loss", is teal with dashed markers and a dashed line style; it starts at approximately 1.1 x 10<sup>1</sup> at Step 0, decreases to approximately 3.5 x 10<sup>0</sup> at Step 10000, and remains relatively stable around 3.2 x 10<sup>0</sup> to 3.3 x 10<sup>0</sup> for the remainder of the x-axis.
